summary: Okta role mapping precedence prevents service-broker impersonation passing delegated runbook role
description:
Issue summary: After an Okta attribute-mapping rollout that introduced a new departmental claim, service-broker token exchanges for delegated users no longer include the 'runbook:editor' role claim. Impact: Oncall and SRE engineers cannot escalate or edit runbooks via the service-broker UI; attempts to perform impersonation actions return 403. Affects all users in the affected Okta group mappings in us-west production.

Impact: 6 oncall engineers reported inability to open or modify runbooks during incident triage; manual workarounds required (temporary role grants). This increased mean time to mitigate for two P1 incidents.

Environment: production (us-west), primary identity provider: Okta, service-broker runs on k8s cluster sb-prod-2, token exchange endpoint /v1/impersonate.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Ensure user is member of 'oncall-sre' Okta group and has department attribute set to 'platform-ops'.
2) Call POST /v1/impersonate with X-Forwarded-User set to service account and include delegated user id in body.
3) Inspect returned JWT (id/access token) for 'roles' claim.

Observed behavior: JWT returned by service-broker does not contain 'runbook:editor' role despite user being in oncall group; UI returns 403 when attempting to edit runbooks.

Expected behavior: Delegated impersonation flow should merge claims from Okta group mappings and delegated role rules so that the impersonated token includes 'runbook:editor' when user is oncall.

Initial hypothesis: New Okta attribute-to-role mapping rule introduced during recent rollout has higher precedence and overrides group mappings, effectively stripping delegated runbook roles during token pack. Alternatively, token assembly code in service-broker may be filtering attribute-based claims when the 'department' attribute is present.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Create test user alice.test@redwood.com and add to 'oncall-sre' group and set Okta profile.department=platform-ops.
2. Use service-broker dev tool: curl -X POST https://sb-prod-2.redwood.internal/v1/impersonate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>' -d '{"delegate":"alice.test@redwood.com"}'.
3. Decode returned JWT (jwt.io) and check 'roles' array.
4. Confirm UI shows 403 when alice.test attempts to edit runbook.
investigation_notes:
- Correlation ID from failing request: cor-20260311-9f7c3b (logs collected from sb-prod-2).
- Identity service trace shows Okta->SCIM sync job ran at 2026-03-11T01:12:05Z; mapping rule 'dept_to_role_v2' was deployed in that window.
- Decoded JWT from a failing impersonation contains attributes.department but lacks any role entries sourced from group mapping.
- Replayed token assembly locally with identical inputs: when dept attribute present, role merger picks attribute precedence and drops group-derived roles.
- Reviewed Okta mapping rules: 'dept_to_role_v2' has explicit mapping for department=platform-ops -> [] (empty) due to old QA placeholder. That rule is marked 'Active' and sits above group-mapping in mapping order.
- No errors in service-broker logs indicating failure to read Okta response; behavior appears deliberate per current mapping precedence logic.

comments: 2026-03-11 - Support (Maya): Customer-facing impact observed during two P1 incidents; raised internal ticket, assigned to identity team.

2026-03-11 - Identity (Ravi): Confirmed 'dept_to_role_v2' was pushed in the 01:10 deploy and has an empty mapping for 'platform-ops' that unintentionally strips roles. Investigating how this rule was promoted from QA.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Liam): Applied temporary override in identity-service config to prefer group-derived roles over department mapping for impersonation flows. Deployed to sb-prod-2 and verified test token now contains 'runbook:editor'. Rolling change to other clusters next.
2026-03-11 - Oncall (A. Ruiz): Verified ability to edit and lift runbook post-override; still recommending a permanent fix to mapping rules order.

2026-03-12 - Identity (Ravi): Created PR to remove placeholder empty-mapping and add unit tests that prevent empty-role mappings from taking precedence. PR: https://github.com/redwood/identity/pull/8721
resolution: Temporary workaround: identity-service config override applied to prefer group mappings during impersonation; manual role grants used for affected users during mitigation window. Next steps: revert dept_to_role_v2 empty mapping and make mapping precedence explicit for impersonation endpoints. Permanent fix pending in PR linked below.
follow_up_actions: 1) Merge PR to remove empty mapping and add guardrails (identity team). 2) Add integration test for impersonation token assembly to CI (platform-test). 3) Schedule postmortem with product and SRE to review deploy gating for identity mapping changes. 4) Notify support and oncall channels when deploy occurs.
